question: The part of the northern plains of India comprising older alluvium is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is **'Bhangar'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhangar is** older alluvial soil** which represents the **upland alluvial tract.**
 
• The soil is rich in** humus** and it gives a high yield due to rich amount of** minerals and humus** in the soil.
 
• It comprises **calcium carbonate** nodules called** 'Kankars'** which are impure in nature.
 
• These soils are **coarser **in texture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khadar -** This is the **new soil** formed due to alluvial deposits along the course of the river, The land slit comprises **silt, mud, clay, and sand and are finer in nature.**
 
• **Bhabar -** The rivers, after descending from the mountains deposits **pebbles** in a narrow belt of about** 8 to 16 km in width** lying parallel to the slopes of Shiwaliks forming Bhabar.
 
• **Terai - **South of bhabar belt, the streams and rivers re-emerge and create a wet, swampy, and marshy region known as Terai. **Dudhwa National Park** lies in this region.
